title: Oracle Prepares Fresh Layoffs That Could Axe 3,000 Jobs in India as AI Spending Soars
excerpt: The database giant is reportedly cutting 7,000 to 10,000 roles globally as it redirects billions toward cloud and AI infrastructure, with India bearing a significant share of the reductions.
body:
• Oracle is preparing to cut approximately 3,000 jobs in India as part of a global restructuring that could eliminate 7,000 to 10,000 roles, according to Moneycontrol and The Economic Times.
  • The cuts come as Oracle redirects spending toward AI infrastructure, having committed $55.7 billion in capital expenditure in fiscal 2026 — up from $21.2 billion a year earlier.
  • Oracle's workforce has already shrunk 13% in the past year, from 162,000 to approximately 141,000, with 21,000 roles eliminated during fiscal 2026.
  • The layoffs mirror a wider pattern across Big Tech, where companies are slashing traditional roles while pouring billions into AI data centres, cloud capacity and GPU clusters.

September 1 Looms as Key Date

Oracle is reportedly planning another round of job cuts that could affect up to 3,000 employees in India, according to a report by Moneycontrol citing officials familiar with the development. Internally discussed figures suggest the company may cut between 7,000 and 10,000 jobs worldwide, with India — home to around 30,000 Oracle employees across Bengaluru, Noida, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune — bearing a significant share.

https://x.com/livemint/status/2094753549972643924

Industry experts identified September 1 as a potential trigger date, with managers reportedly asked to identify roles that could be eliminated ahead of Oracle's second fiscal quarter. However, some reports have also pointed to September 15 as another possible timeline. Oracle has not publicly confirmed the layoffs.

Pareekh Jain, chief executive of market research firm EIIRTrend, estimated that the latest job cuts could affect between 2,000 and 3,000 employees in India, with the reductions expected to begin in early September.

Where Oracle's Money Is Moving

The reported cuts come against a backdrop of record-breaking investment in AI infrastructure. Oracle reported $67.4 billion in revenue for fiscal 2026, up 17% year-on-year. Cloud revenue rose 39% to $34 billion, while cloud infrastructure revenue jumped 77% to $18.1 billion. In the fourth quarter alone, cloud infrastructure revenue surged 93%.

But sustaining that growth is expensive. Capital expenditure jumped to $55.7 billion in fiscal 2026 from $21.2 billion a year earlier, driven largely by data-centre expansion. The company generated a record $32 billion in operating cash flow, up 54%, but its investment programme consumed far more — leaving Oracle with negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion.

"The AI bubble is actually an OpenAI bubble. If it collapses, it could become the Lehman Brothers of the AI bubble."

— Ed Zitron, AI researcher and critic

OpenAI's growing demand has become a central factor in Oracle's infrastructure push. The two companies have signed a $300 billion, five-year contract for computing capacity. Elon Musk's xAI also uses Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to run its Grok models. In February 2026, Oracle announced plans to raise up to $50 billion through debt and equity financing to support demand from customers including Nvidia, Meta, OpenAI and TikTok.

Oracle ended fiscal 2026 with $638 billion in remaining performance obligations, up 363% from the previous year, with much of the increase coming from large AI contracts signed during the second half.

A Pattern Across Big Tech

Oracle is not alone in cutting traditional roles while ramping AI spending. Microsoft has reportedly placed around 500 employees in India on performance improvement plans, with estimates suggesting roughly 2% of its Indian workforce could be affected. The PIP process, however, does not necessarily lead to termination — a Microsoft spokesperson said employees who fall short of expectations may be offered coaching, placed on a PIP, given voluntary separation options, or terminated.

The broader pattern is unmistakable. Amazon, Microsoft and Meta have all laid off thousands as part of cost-cutting drives aimed at freeing capital for AI infrastructure investment. For Oracle specifically, the workforce fell 13% in a single year, from about 162,000 to 141,000 as of May 31, 2026. Sales and marketing saw the largest reduction, with nearly 6,000 jobs cut, while hardware roles — linked to Oracle's expanding infrastructure ambitions — were comparatively preserved.

What This Means for India's Tech Workforce

If the fresh round materialises, as much as 10% of Oracle's 30,000-strong Indian workforce would have been eliminated. India is a major hub for Oracle, with large engineering, cloud, support and technology operations based across the country.

The layoffs add to a challenging period for India's IT workforce. While demand for AI, cloud and data engineering skills remains strong, traditional roles in support, testing and legacy system maintenance are being consolidated or automated. For Indian tech professionals with Oracle experience, the message is clear: roles tied to legacy infrastructure are shrinking, while those connected to cloud, AI and data centres are growing — but the transition is neither smooth nor painless.
